newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank to borrow up to $1.6 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank to borrow up to $1.6 bln in 1997.

text.p: Romania's National Bank (BNR) will continue prudent borrowing policies in 1997 when it will draw up to $1.6 billion and seek better terms for its international borrowing, BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said.
"We plan to raise up to $1.6 billion from world markets, maybe less," Isarescu told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
"Our first aim is to upgrade what we have achieved so far. We seek longer maturities and lower costs for our raisings."
Romania rejoined world capital markets in 1995 after more than a decade of isolation imposed by the former communist government.

The BNR sought to build up its hard currency reserves by launching its first Samurai and Eurobond issues -- of three and five years -- last year, after Romania got ratings from major credit rating agencies.
In 1996 the BNR borrowed around $1.4 billion from world markets and serviced debt payments of around $1.2 billion, and its reserves rose to $855.3 million by year-end.
